items.title: Week in review: Do Monday check-ins prompt Sunday scaries?
items.summary: We’re rounding up last week’s stories, including an Internal Revenue Service regulation addressing auto-enrollment to retirement plans.

items.title: Executives get more AI training than other workers, hurting adoption, report finds
items.summary: The disparity may explain why some employers see a “stalled transformation” within their enterprises, according to researchers at Marsh.

items.title: Employers should prepare for a labor market shake-up in 2027, Indeed and Glassdoor say
items.summary: Higher turnover and a need for a better leadership pipeline may be big concerns for talent leaders in the coming year, the hiring platforms predicted.

items.title: Job candidates’ AI usage is obscuring their viability, report finds
items.summary: Nine in 10 employers worry they rejected a real applicant because they mistakenly believed a resume was fake or artificial intelligence-generated, according to a new study.

items.title: Bipartisan bill aims to secure more FMLA time for parents with NICU babies
items.summary: Supporters pointed to parents having to decide between using job-protected time to stay with their preterm newborn or for bonding later.

items.title: How to tackle employee pay cynicism
items.summary: Part of the solution is enhanced transparency “when you’ve got a good story to tell,” a global rewards solution leader said.

items.title: DOL flips independent contractor switch back with new final rule
items.summary: Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling said the agency’s renewed “economic reality” test would provide greater clarity to both workers and employers.

items.title: Work done outside regular hours may count toward FMLA eligibility
items.summary: In an opinion letter, DOL also said that if accurate time records are not available, eligibility sometimes must be assumed.
